title: Duke Ellington's rise and Henderson's lead
summary: Scott and Albertson discuss Ellington as an upcoming rival and how few big bands existed in New York.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: He had taken over the band from (inaudible) at that point.
No, he had his own band. He had his own band. I don't know whether he took it over from Snowden or not, because when I joined he had his own band.
And did Fletcher see Duke as a threat, an upcoming rival?

No, see, it wasn't so many bands in New York then, like it turned out later. Because, after that, they started coming in all directions, far and wide, far and wide. Big bands started opening up. The Dorsey Brothers hadn't come there then. Benny Goodman wasn't thought of, and Harry James wasn't thought of.
Well, a lot of big bands, they came later. And all on the strength of Fletcher having a big band. Well, naturally, some of those bands had more backing than he had, and they could make it, see.
